FOCUSMAIL / YOUR INFORMATION

Privacy, in plain words.

What the app stores, when information is shared, and the choices you control.

Privacy policy · Last updated 20 October 2026

Email management happens on your computer and with your mail provider. Optional AI requests share selected email content with the endpoint you configure, only when you ask for those features.
1. Who this policy covers2. Information the desktop app uses3. Google and Microsoft account access4. When information leaves your computer5. Optional AI processing6. Retention, removal, and revocation7. This website and technical records8. Changes and contact

1. Who this policy covers

This policy describes the current FocusMail desktop beta and this informational website. FocusMail is an email client that helps people process one conversation at a time. The project’s support and privacy contact is diemme89@gmail.com.

The desktop app stores its working data on your computer. It does not require a separate FocusMail cloud account or route your mailbox through a FocusMail-operated mail server. You choose which mail accounts and optional AI services to connect.

2. Information the desktop app uses

  • Account information: your email address, account name, mail-server settings, and provider identity information needed for sign-in.
  • Authentication: OAuth access and refresh tokens for connected Google or Microsoft accounts, or IMAP/SMTP passwords or app passwords. API keys for your chosen AI server are also stored locally.
  • Email data: message identifiers, senders and recipients, subjects, dates, message text and links, and thread/folder information. The app imports inbox mail and limits imported Sent history to the last 24 hours.
  • Local app data: preferences, saved delegation contacts, snooze times, local action history and achievements, and cached AI priority results and submission-attempt records.

Message bodies and general settings are kept in a local database. Credentials and tokens are encrypted using a key stored with the local app profile. This is not end-to-end encryption of the mailbox, and someone with access to your computer and profile may be able to access its data. Protect your device and backups.

3. Google and Microsoft account access

When you connect Google or Microsoft, sign-in and consent take place on the provider’s website. FocusMail receives authorization tokens; it does not receive your Google or Microsoft account password through that sign-in flow.

Google mail access uses the https://mail.google.com/ permission required by the app’s IMAP/SMTP integration. It enables reading and organizing mail and sending replies or forwards at your request. Microsoft uses delegated IMAP and SMTP permissions and offline access to keep sign-in available across sessions.

Mail is fetched only when you press Sync inbox. Tokens may be refreshed to carry out requested account operations. Reading cached mail, startup, and ordinary queue updates do not trigger automatic mail fetching.

FocusMail’s use and transfer of information received from Google APIs will adhere to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including its Limited Use requirements. Google user data is used to provide the email features you request, not for advertising, sale, or training generalized AI or machine-learning models by FocusMail.

4. When information leaves your computer

Action you chooseRecipient and information shared
Connect or sync an accountYour mail provider receives sign-in, token-refresh, and mail requests. Mail data is downloaded to the local app.
Send a replyYour sending mail provider and the addressed recipient receive your reply and the headers needed to deliver and thread it.
Delegate an emailYour sending provider and the person you select receive your note and the latest received message’s text, links, and forwarded headers. Attachments are not included.
Ask the thinking partnerThe AI API endpoint you configure receives your question, relevant discussion history, and selected-thread content, including subject, sender details, dates, and message text. The current implementation bounds this context to portions of up to eight messages and recent chat turns.
Prioritize inboxThe configured AI endpoint receives each new individual email’s subject, sender, date, and bounded message text, plus classification instructions. Common quoted history is excluded where detectable.
Contact supportThe support email account receives the message and information you choose to send.

There is no automatic switch to a different AI server if your configured server fails. Google/Microsoft approval and workplace policies still apply to account access.

5. Optional AI processing

AI is optional. Without an AI key or configured service, you can still read and manage your mail. AI requests happen when you ask the thinking partner or confirm manual inbox prioritization; syncing alone does not send mail to AI.

The AI service is the endpoint you select in Preferences. Its operator may be OpenAI, another provider, or your own server. That provider’s terms, privacy policy, retention practices, and processing locations apply to the data you send. Choose a service appropriate for the contents of your email and compatible with applicable Google user-data restrictions. We do not claim that every custom endpoint has the same privacy protections.

FocusMail does not use email content to train its own models or generalized AI models. Optional AI calls are made to deliver the requested assistance. AI replies and priority suggestions can be inaccurate; drafts require your review before sending.

For prioritization, the local database records an attempt before sending. Recorded emails are not automatically resent during sync, restart, or a model change. A timeout or interruption can leave no result even if the provider received the message. Different app profiles or computers keep separate records. This once-per-email ledger applies to prioritization, not to separate chat questions you initiate.

6. Retention, removal, and revocation

Local email and app data stay in the app profile until you remove them or the app prunes them. Older locally cached Sent messages are pruned on manual sync; the provider’s copies are not deleted by that pruning.

  • Manage connected accounts in Settings and revoke provider access when you no longer want the app to connect. For complete removal of local mail and credentials, delete the local app profile as described below. This does not delete the mailbox at your provider.
  • Revoke authorization through your Google account connections or the relevant Microsoft account or organization settings. Removing an account locally is separate from revoking the provider’s grant.
  • Remove an AI key in Preferences to delete that locally saved key. Previously submitted data remains subject to the AI provider’s retention and deletion processes.
  • Delete the app’s local data profile after quitting the app to remove remaining local preferences, saved people, encrypted credential material, and priority-attempt records. Uninstalling the app alone may leave its data profile behind. Backups may retain copies separately.

Priority-attempt fingerprints and results may remain after account removal so previously submitted email is not resent if the account is re-added. Delete the complete local profile to remove these records. For help locating your profile or addressing a support message you sent us, contact diemme89@gmail.com. Do not send passwords or tokens to support.

7. This website and technical records

This website provides product, support, and privacy information. It does not ask you to log in to a mailbox or upload email. The pages do not contain advertising trackers, analytics scripts, a mailing-list form, or third-party font requests.

The hosting provider may process normal request information, such as IP address, browser details, requested URLs, and timestamps, to deliver and secure the website under its own policies. If hosted on GitHub Pages, see GitHub’s privacy statement. Email links open your email application; no support message is sent just by viewing a page.

The desktop app may write diagnostic logs locally to troubleshoot connection failures. If you share logs for support, review them first and avoid including private message content or credentials.

8. Changes and contact

We may update this policy as the beta changes. The date at the top identifies the current version. Material changes to data handling should be described before the affected feature is used.

For privacy questions, deletion help, or support, contact the FocusMail project at diemme89@gmail.com.
